title: Clean and Split Text
content:
What problem does this solve?
Realistic programs accept text with extra spaces and mixed case. String methods help normalize and separate fields. strip() returns a new string without surrounding whitespace; lower() returns lowercase for robust comparisons; split(separator) returns a list of pieces. Strings do not change in place — save or return the method result.

Previously in your program
You built and read strings with f-strings, and returned structured values from functions. Now you return cleaned text and parse one well-formed record.

Basic syntax
  command = "  NORTH  "
  cleaned = command.strip().lower()
  parts = "Mira|Scout".split("|")

What actually happens
Methods like strip, lower, and split return new strings or lists. Reassign a variable or return the method result to use the change.

When this is useful
Normalize commands and names before comparing. Split simple records so later code can work with labeled pieces.
concepts: strip() removes surrounding whitespace and returns a new string
lower() returns lowercase for robust comparisons
split(separator) returns a list of pieces
Strings are immutable — methods return new values

examples.title: Normalize one command
examples.explanation: Method calls return a new, cleaned string; the original name still refers to the unmodified text.

common_mistakes: Calling a method without saving the returned string
Forgetting to strip spaces before comparing text
Using split without a separator when a specific character separates fields

command = "  OPEN GATE  "
command.strip()
command.lower()
print(command)
hints: String methods return new strings; they do not change the old one.
Reassign a variable to the cleaned result before printing.
You may chain calls or do them in two steps.

tests.message: After the fix, the printed line should be open gate.

exercises.title: Transfer task: normalize a username
exercises.prompt: Write normalize_username(text) that returns the text with surrounding whitespace removed and all letters lowercase.
hints: Call strip() and lower() on the parameter.
Either order is fine for behavior here.

tests.name: normalize_username
tests.message: Define normalize_username(text) with exactly one parameter.
A simple name should be lowercased.
Only spaces should become an empty string.

exercises.title: Parse one log line
exercises.prompt: Write parse_log_line(line) for a well-formed "name|status" line. Return {"name": <trimmed name>, "status": <trimmed lowercase status>}.
hints: Strip both pieces; lowercase the status.
Return a dictionary with keys name and status.

tests.message: Split the input line inside parse_log_line so both fields are available.
Strip surrounding spaces from the pieces inside parse_log_line.
Lowercase the status text inside parse_log_line.
Trim the name and lowercase the status.
Lowercase the status and preserve the name.
Spaces around either field should be removed.
Do not hardcode names or statuses — parse the given text.
